A split diagram titled "Factors affecting a maize plant". Left side (Abiotic factors): A bright sun with rays pointing to the leaves (Light/Temperature), a rain cloud with raindrops (Rainfall), wavy lines blowing the stalk (Wind), and a cutaway of the soil showing layers and water droplets (Soil texture/Moisture). Right side (Biotic factors): A caterpillar chewing a leaf (Pest), a weed growing next to the maize (Competition), spots on a leaf with a magnified fungal spore (Disease), and an earthworm in the soil (Beneficial soil organism).

A map of Nigeria or West Africa shaded in horizontal bands to show the ecological zones. The southernmost edge along the coast is dark green (Mangrove Swamp). Above it is green (Rainforest). The next band is light green (Derived Savanna). The wide middle section is yellow-green (Guinea Savanna). The northern section is orange-yellow (Sudan Savanna), and the extreme northeast corner is pale yellow (Sahel Savanna). A small purple patch in the middle shows the Montane region (Jos Plateau). A compass rose and a legend matching the colours to the zone names.
